newsitem.title: UK: Etam sees improvement in current trading.
newsitem.headline: Etam sees improvement in current trading.

text.p: Womenswear retailer Etam Plc said on Thursday trading in the current financial year was improving with like-for-like sales up by two percent and full price merchandise six percent ahead of last year.
"Acceptable levels of profitability will only be sustained by full price sales growth and it is encouraging that progress is now being made," the company said in its results statement.
Etam last year expressed concern about the steady increase in markdown sales as a proportion of total sales which it said was "not sustainable" as a mode of trading.

The mix of markdown sales as a proportion of total sales has now been restored to more normal levels and more than 80 percent of turnover is being generated from full-price merchandise which the company said was "a significant turnaround which reinforces the merchandise and trading strategies being pursued".
Etam reported a loss after tax for the year to January 25 of 4.22 million stg compared with a loss of 0.24 million the year before. It maintained a total dividend of 1.25 pence per share.

"Bearing in mind the magnitude of the problems inherent in the business and the massive changes that have been brought about, it is clear that progress is being made in the quest for sustainable and quality turnover and profit growth," said chairman Stanley Lewis. "However, much remains to be done".
